Methods for zinbreg fits

Source: R/methods.R
zinbreg-methods.Rd

Standard S3 methods for objects returned by zinbreg().

Usage

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
print(x, digits = max(3L, getOption("digits") - 3L), ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary.zinbreg'
print(x, digits = max(3L, getOption("digits") - 3L), ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
coef(object, model = c("full", "count", "zero"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
vcov(object, model = c("full", "count", "zero"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
logLik(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
nobs(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
fitted(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
residuals(object, type = c("response", "pearson"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
predict(
  object,
  newdata = NULL,
  type = c("response", "count", "zero", "prob0"),
  ...
)

Arguments

digits

Number of significant digits to print.

...

Not used.

object, x

A "zinbreg" object (or its summary for print).

model

For coef() and vcov(): "full" (both parts, named count_* and zero_* as in pscl::zeroinfl()), "count" or "zero".

type

For residuals(): "response" (\(y - (1-\hat\pi)\hat\mu\)) or "pearson" (divided by \(\sqrt{\mathrm{Var}(Y)}\) with \(\mathrm{Var}(Y) = (1-\pi)\mu\{1 + \mu(\pi + 1/\theta)\}\)). For predict(): "response" (\((1-\hat\pi)\hat\mu\)), "count" (\(\hat\mu\)), "zero" (\(\hat\pi\)) or "prob0" (\(P(Y=0) = \hat\pi + (1-\hat\pi)f_{NB}(0;\hat\mu,\hat\theta)\)).

newdata

Optional data frame to predict for.

Value

As for nbreg-methods. logLik() has df = number of count and zero coefficients + 1.

Examples

set.seed(3)
n <- 400
d <- data.frame(x = rnorm(n), z = rnorm(n))
d$y <- ifelse(rbinom(n, 1, plogis(-0.5 + d$z)) == 1, 0,
              rnbinom(n, size = 2, mu = exp(1 + 0.5 * d$x)))
fit <- zinbreg(y ~ x | z, data = d)
coef(fit)
#> count_(Intercept)           count_x  zero_(Intercept)            zero_z 
#>         1.0112410         0.4266714        -0.5951456         0.8375193 
coef(fit, model = "zero")
#> (Intercept)           z 
#>  -0.5951456   0.8375193 
AIC(fit)
#> [1] 1396.044
nd <- data.frame(x = 0, z = c(-1, 0, 1))
predict(fit, newdata = nd, type = "response")
#>        1        2        3 
#> 2.219321 1.771861 1.208744 
predict(fit, newdata = nd, type = "zero")
#>         1         2         3 
#> 0.1926838 0.3554551 0.5602985
